before.summary: Cleveland Clinic reported that its Phase 1 trial of an investigational vaccine targeting α-lactalbumin found an immune response in 74% of 35 participants. The vaccine was described as safe and well tolerated, with mostly mild injection-site skin inflammation. A Phase 2 study is planned to assess efficacy.

after.summary: Cleveland Clinic reported an immune response in 74% of 35 Phase 1 participants. The study included people at risk of recurrence after triple-negative breast cancer treatment and cancer-free people with inherited risk; one cohort also received pembrolizumab. The report described tolerability and dose finding, not demonstrated cancer prevention. It said a Phase 2 efficacy study was planned for late 2026.

identity_review.reason: Use the registry-named candidate, preserving the preventive aim and mixed cohorts. Zymosan is identified by the registry as the vaccine adjuvant, not a separate investigated treatment. The standalone vaccine cohorts support this identity even though one additional cohort receives standard-of-care pembrolizumab. Immune response is not evidence that cancer was prevented. No trial or claim approval performed by this correction.

trial_review.assessment: Compatible. Registry prevention cohort explicitly studies cancer-free individuals with genetic risk; other cohorts study recurrence risk after treatment. Zymosan is the vaccine preparation adjuvant. A pembrolizumab cohort does not negate the standalone vaccine cohorts. The article names this exact registration.
trial_review.outcomes: Three maximum-tolerated-dose outcomes at Day 84; no cancer-prevention efficacy result inferred. Six bounded readings retain exact record wording.
trial_review.results: Posted 2026-07-17; multi-row treatment outcome keeps numbers hidden, other cohorts retain NA. Posted results do not advance the phase.

paper_review.assessment: Primary conference abstract confirms NCT04674306 and the same preventive/recurrence cohorts. It explicitly says Phase I cannot establish clinical efficacy. Metadata-only related paper, not the source of the 2025 final percentages.

Indexed title and institutional identity match this earlier Phase I vaccine report. Publisher full text was unavailable; retain as a metadata-only related conference abstract, without inferred results.

statements.reason: The report supports the 74% immune-response statement across cohorts. Earlier mouse result remains pending. Summary avoids a blanket safety conclusion or demonstrated prevention.

efficiency.optional_source_limit: GSRS development-code discovery did not answer after four attempts. No unchanged full preparation repeat.
